Negative Appraisals.value: I have permanently changed for the worse
The event happened because of the way I acted
I acted in ways that go against who I am

vignette: Sofía, a 27-year-old Latin American animator, has been struggling with the aftermath of physical abuse inflicted by her former romantic partner. The trauma has left deep emotional scars and has fundamentally altered how she views herself and the world around her. The incident occurred about six months ago when Sofía was still in an on-again-off-again relationship with Carlos. One evening, after a particularly heated argument, he lost control and physically attacked her. The violence was unexpected and devastating, leaving Sofía feeling profoundly vulnerable and shattered. Since that day, she has been plagued by the belief that she is permanently changed for the worse. Sofía’s self-blame is a constant companion in her thoughts, gnawing at her sense of peace every time she recalls the event. She often wonders if the abuse happened because of something she did or said, feeling responsible despite the clear fault being with Carlos. This belief has created a heavy weight on her shoulders, making it difficult for her to move forward and trust others. Her values have also been shaken to their core. Sofía prides herself on her integrity and the strength of character she brings to every relationship and professional setting. After the abuse, however, she felt that she compromised these values by staying in a toxic environment for so long. This violation has left her feeling like she no longer recognizes the person she once was. Sofía’s occupation as an animator has become less fulfilling since the incident. Her creativity often dries up when she faces deadlines and tight schedules, reminding her of the control issues that led to the abuse. The stress at work makes it harder for her to shake off the feeling of being permanently damaged. She finds herself isolating from colleagues and avoiding social gatherings with friends, fearing that others might see her as weak or damaged. The turning point came when Sofía realized she was starting to isolate herself completely. Her once vibrant life has become muted, filled with a constant sense of dread and self-criticism. The weight of feeling permanently changed for the worse is overwhelming. She knows she needs help but is afraid that acknowledging her struggles will further validate her belief that she is damaged beyond repair. Sofía’s hope lies in finding a way to reclaim her identity and trust herself again, despite the deep wounds left by Carlos's abuse. She hopes therapy can help her see that while the experience was traumatic, it does not define her entirely, and that there is still room for healing and growth. As she seeks help, Sofía’s most pressing fear is being seen as permanently broken. Her hope, however, is to regain a sense of self-worth and trust in her own strength and resilience. She wants to believe that she can move past this and lead a fulfilling life again.
